neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 1.1 encodes pairwise shift interactions through capped inverse separations, then generalizes Soundararajan's tail-distribution method from one log-zeta value to a weighted sum of shifted log-zeta values.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A short Dirichlet-polynomial proxy turns a moment lower bound into an energy quotient
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The zeta-product is approximated by a short coefficient polynomial A(t); a smoothed correlation S1 and its quadratic energy S2 are combined by Cauchy-Schwarz so the desired moment is bounded below by S1 squared over S2.

section_entries.label: Random-matrix conjecture for shifted moments
section_entries.mathematical_role: Derives the three separation regimes by contour rescaling, pole splitting, balanced allocations, and a finite-scale determinant limit.

unit_result_entry.title: Finite scaled separation is encoded by a continuous determinant limit
unit_result_entry.why_material: At nonzero finite matrix-scaled separation, the same rescaling leads to a sine-kernel determinant divided by a Vandermonde factor; continuous extension defines the interpolation constant between the two extreme regimes.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This unit states the critical-scale case and explicitly defers existence of the collision limit to Appendix 5.1.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Separated pole families are dominated by balanced contour allocations
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: For separation larger than the inverse matrix scale, each contour is split around two pole families. Power counting shows that only allocations with equal numbers assigned to each family survive at leading order, causing factorization into two ordinary moments times a separation factor.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A covariance parameter controls Gaussian and large-deviation tails
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The moment is written as an integral of joint-tail measure, and Theorem 3.1 packages all shift interaction into W, giving Gaussian-like decay through the moderate range and stronger exponential decay for extreme values.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Both the random-matrix and Dirichlet-series analyses first enclose a cluster of nearby singularities as one object; rescaling, Laurent extraction, or divided differences then produce a finite limit without treating colliding poles independently.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The contour integrals and determinant quotient live in different calculations; this is a shared conceptual move, not an identity between their local constants.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Coalescing singularities are handled by local compression before taking limits
